answer: You have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a main reimbursement claim [1][2], or 15 days under the 2024 archived rules [3]. Additionally, group claims have a submission window of 60 days from discharge [5].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan [1][2].
The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail plans, whereas it is 24 months for the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above [3][5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days [1].
Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals as of 1 April 2026 [1].

According to the Aurora Gold plan terms, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100%, and the bonus is not reduced by a claim [1]. However, the plan comparison overview states that the no-claim bonus on Gold is 25% per year with a maximum of 100% [5], while another source for the Aurora Gold plan states it is 25% per claim-free year accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment, as it is listed as a permanent treatment-related exclusion. [1]
The cataract surgery sub-limit on Gold is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome or receive no response within 15 days, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. Furthermore, if Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory or they do not respond within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

The ambulance cover includes road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, the Aurora Gold plan provides air ambulance cover of ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The 30-day initial waiting period applies, but no separate waiting period is required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. It lasts for 15 days from the receipt of the policy document (or 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing) [1][2].
You get 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is defined as a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation because of technological advancement, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
A hospital must notify Aurora of an emergency admission for cashless within 24 hours [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA). [1]
To qualify as a hospital, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid [1][5]. Because your room rent of ₹15,000 per day exceeds your Silver limit of ₹10,000 per day (2% of your ₹5,00,000 sum insured), a proportionate deduction applies to your claim [1][2][5].

Dependent parents can be covered on the Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, but they are not allowed on the Bronze plan [1]. Because the premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered, adding a dependent parent to a floater often costs more than an individual senior-citizen policy for that parent [4].
